MAPPING: data/malinowska_2021_saq.py takes item codes straight from the S1 Data column names (strip/lower/space->underscore, so 'KIER 24A' -> kier_24a) -- no positional step -- but the XLSX header row carries codes only, no wording, so the code->question tie is the numeric suffix against the questionnaire's own printed item numbers 1-36. That tie is corroborated by the source paper's explicit number->subscale assignment (TC 1-6, SC 7-13, JS 15-19, SR 20-23, PM 24-28, WC 29-32, q14 = management, q33-36 = interdisciplinary collaboration) and its statement that questions 2, 11 and 36 are reverse scored; both reproduce in the data (see verification row and verify_malinowska_2021_saq_physicians.R). MANAGEMENT PAIRS: questions 24-28 are each rated twice, once for the ward manager and once for the hospital director (questionnaire footnote: '* W pytaniach od 24 do 28 prosze o wyrazanie opinii zarowno w odniesieniu do kierownika oddzialu jak i dyrektora szpitala.'). kier_24a..kier_28a are read as the ward-manager column and bezp_24..bezp_28 as the hospital-director column, on three converging grounds: the source column name 'KIER <n>A' matches the printed response-column label 'kier. oddzialu'; the questionnaire prints that column first and the XLSX interleaves KIER <n>A immediately before bezp_<n>; and the kier_* items average 73.08 on the 0-100 conversion against 45.97 for bezp_24-28, the direction SAQ studies consistently report. The referent is carried in item_text as a bracketed editorial addition ('... [kier. oddzialu]' / '... [dyr. szpitala]'), which is a deviation from the printed stem and is disclosed here and in the public_note. RESP: 1-5 are the A-E anchors and 6 is the questionnaire's 'Nie dotyczy' / X option -- the source paper states '1 = strongly disagree (A); 2 = rather disagree (B); 3 = neutral answer (C); 4 = quite agree (D); 5 = strongly agree (E)' and that 'For each question, the questionnaire authors included the "does not concern" option'; resp=6 is 1.7% of responses overall and concentrated on bezp_35 (122 of 738), the pharmacist item, which is what a not-applicable code should look like. TRANSCRIPTION DEVIATIONS, all deliberate: item 13 ships the source's own typo 'ulawia' (for 'ulatwia'); item 36 ships 'prowadza' as printed (grammatically 'prowadzace'); item 15 is the only stem not recoverable byte-for-byte from the PDF text layer, because the 'SAFETY CLIMATE' section watermark overprints it ('Lubie mojaCLIMATE prace.'), and 'Lubie moja prace.' is what is shipped; the three instruction sentences are three separate spans of the form's header, each verbatim, concatenated in reading order. TRANSLATION: translation_source=mixed -- item_text_translated, option_text_translated and instructions_translated are the UT SAQ-SF's own English (a parallel version, so it diverges from the Polish adaptation in places: q1 Polish reads 'Praca pielegniarek w moim oddziale jest postrzegana pozytywnie' where the original reads 'Nurse input is well received in this clinical area', and q27 Polish reads 'Problemy personelu...' = staff problems where the original reads 'Problem personnel...'); section_prompt_translated is the only field IRW translated itself, because the referent footnote is specific to the Polish form and has no counterpart on the UT form. RIGHTS: no reserved right locatable, so the 2026-09-05/2026-09-08 test does not fire. The instrument rights holder's own page states, under the heading 'Permissions', 'You have our permission to use the short form of the Safety Attitudes Questionnaire. Complete this form to request a permission letter.' -- a blanket grant followed by an optional documentation mechanism, with no fee, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause anywhere on the page; the UT form itself carries only a bare copyright notice ('Copyright (c) 2004 by The University of Texas at Austin'), which under the PANAS reading is a notice, not a term. The Polish adaptation, which is the wording actually shipped, was published by its own rights holder in a CC BY 4.0 PLOS supplement and its footer reads '2017 Iwona Malinowska-Lipien, Uniwersytet Jagiellonski-Collegium Medicum za zgoda The University of Texas at Austin' ('with the consent of'). No row was added to itemtext/instrument_rights_register.csv from this agent because a sibling table on the same instrument (malinowska_2021_saq_nurses) was being processed concurrently and the register is a shared file -- the SAQ is worth a register row and the orchestrator should add one. STEP 3b: clean. 41 live items = 36 SAQ-SF questions plus the 5 second-referent management ratings, resp 1-6, matching the dictionary Description; the demographic bezp_d_* columns were excluded by the processing script and are not in the table.

The English for those ten items' section prompt was translated by IRW; every other English field is the University of Texas SAQ-SF's own wording.

note: PASS WITH CAVEATS. (1) item_text is blank for all five items by design. The five items are the RAVLT's five successive immediate-recall trials of one 15-word list -- the same task repeated, so there is no per-item wording, and neither the paper nor the .sav publishes the 15-word stimulus list itself (the article states only that 46 words, '15 words presented to him in the first task together with 31 distractors', were used in the later recognition task). 2026-09-05 picture-stimulus ruling applied: ship the table, leave item_text blank, let the item code carry the trial identity. Nothing was authored to fill it. (2) CODE DERIVATION: exempt, pattern 1. data/mancone_2024_ravlt.py melts the S1 File .sav's own SESS_1..SESS_5 columns by name (var_name='item'), so the IRW item code IS the source column name verbatim; pyreadstat shows the .sav's variable labels are identical to those names ('SESS_1' -> 'SESS_1') and only gender/group/gaming_prevalence carry value labels, so the file holds no item text at either level. (3) TEXT: the only published description of the administration is the paper's third-person Methods prose, shipped verbatim as `instructions` ('The test is made up of seven tasks. In the first task the examiner reads the words and asks the subject to repeat them. After the first task, the words are read another four times and the subject is asked to repeat them, including the previously recited words.'). Nothing was rewritten into second person; no participant-facing script was published. The sentences about the 15-min distraction, the delayed recall and the 46-word recognition task were deliberately NOT shipped: they describe tasks that are not in this table (DELAYED_RECALLS / FALSE_RICOGNITIONSI are excluded by the processing script). (4) RESP: resp is a raw count of words correctly recalled on that trial (0-15), so option_text is blank -- there are no labelled response options. Rows enumerate exactly the levels each item's own respondents used (48 rows: 7/9/11/11/10 for SESS_1..5), not a cross product; the union is the live resp set {3..15}. correct_response is blank: a free-recall count has no per-item key. (5) LANGUAGE: omitted rather than guessed. The paper never states the administration language; the sample is Italian (Cassino, Italy) and the .sav's own labels are Italian ('gruppo', 'eta', 'TOTALE_Ripetizioni'), so the administration was near-certainly Italian -- but no administered wording is shipped at all (item_text blank, instructions are the authors' own English Methods prose, not a translation of anything), so there is no base field for a `_translated` twin to sit beside. Same call as klatt_2016_speed_estimation. (6) STEP 3b: clean. Table name says RAVLT recall; the live items SESS_1..SESS_5 with resp 3-15 are exactly the per-trial correct-recall counts (max 15 words), and the paper's Table 2 speaks of 'the fifth session'. The intrusion-error columns INTRU_1..5 are a separate IRW table and are not here. (7) VERIFICATION (verify_mancone_2024_ravlt_recall.R, VERDICT: PASS): Table 1's per-group immediate-recall mean/SD (12.35/1.73, 8.10/1.43, 10.80/2.02, 12.60/1.22) is reproduced EXACTLY by SESS_5 and by no other item (next closest SESS_4, max|diff| 1.25), and Table 2's six fifth-session group contrasts (-4.25, -1.55, 0.25, 2.70, 4.50, 1.80) reproduce to 0.000. SESS_1..SESS_4 rest on the rising learning curve (6.287 < 7.862 < 9.312 < 10.012 < 10.963) plus the codes' own numbering, so the row is PARTIAL. (8) RIGHTS: nothing to quote, and nothing at risk -- no instrument wording is shipped. The 15-word RAVLT stimulus list is NOT published by this table, so no question arises about the Rey (1958) / Carlesimo et al. (1996) Italian standardisation. The article and its S1 File are CC BY 4.0. (9) AUDIT WARNS EXPECTED: audit_batch.R will WARN '100% of rows have blank item_text | 100% of rows have blank option_text'. Both are correct here per (1) and (4) and neither is retrievable from any source.
